 24-team College Football Playoff bracket seeded based on second 2026 CFP Rankings
 Thomas Goldkamp 54m 0 Share Share 
 After three seasons with a 12-team College Football Playoff field, the format will change in 2027 and move to 24 teams. We wanted to give you a sense of what the doubled playoff field might look like in practice, so we’ve taken tonight’s second set of CFP rankings and applied it to a would-be 24-team field.
 The system will be set up to feature 19 at-large teams and an auto bid for the Power Four champions and the and the highest ranked Group of Six team. As of right now, the Pac-12’s Boise State , ranked No. 24 in the second CFP Rankings, would earn the G6 bid into a hypothetical 24-team College Football Playoff.

 Below is what the expanded 24-team College Football Playoff Bracket would look like, based on the second set of CFP Rankings of the 2026 season. The first and second round games would be played on home fields, hosted by the higher seed.
 Hypothetical 24-team CFP Matchups
 24. Boise State at 9. Indiana
 WINNER TRAVELS TO: 8. Tennessee
 23. Arizona at 10. BYU
 WINNER TRAVELS TO: 7. Miami
 22. Missouri at 11. Kentucky
 WINNER TRAVELS TO: 6. Texas
 21. LSU at 12. Texas Tech
 WINNER TRAVELS TO: 5. Notre Dame
 20. Ohio State at 13. Wake Forest
 WINNER TRAVELS TO: 4. UCLA
 19. Ole Miss at 14. Houston
 WINNER TRAVELS TO: 3. Alabama
 18. USC at 15. Iowa
 WINNER TRAVELS TO: 2. Utah
 17. South Carolina at 16. Oregon
 WINNER TRAVELS TO: 1. Georgia
 College Football Playoff aims for ‘spectacular’ event
 While the move to a 24-team playoff hasn’t been popular in all corners, the College Football Playoff leadership believes it can be a step in the right direction for the sport. The executive director spoke out Monday following the news of the deal for an expanded playoff becoming official.
 He believes the new field is capable of delivering thrilling results for the fans. How that plays out in practice remains to be seen, but he is encouraged by the opportunity.
 “We’re aware of the fan sentiment and that many fans aren’t in favor of expansion. That was certainly weighed into the decision. It was considered,” CFP executive director Rich Clark said. “Ultimately we just need to make a spectacular Playoff. I mean, the CFP has a responsibility to our fans, they’re the lifeblood of college football. We owe it to them to make this great. That really is our intent. We appreciate our fans. We did take into account their sentiment. That was rolled into this decision. But we decided to move forward with it.”
